newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jailed Indonesian labour chief faces medical tests.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Indonesian labour chief faces medical tests.

text.p: Jailed Indonesian labour leader Mucthar Pakpahan, on trial for subversion, will soon undergo tests on a tumour on his right lung, a family member said on Thursday.
"Mucthar has a tumour in the bottom of his right lung," the family member, who asked not to be identified said.
"He is due to have a bronchoscopia test on Friday and a biopsy on Monday," he said. "He's in good spirits."
In the first test the pathways, or bronchi, in the lung will be checked. The second test will involve the removal of a section of the tumour for analysis.
Medical sources said results of the tests to determine if the tumour is benign or malignant could be available by Monday.
Pakpahan was detained last July and charged with subversion, which carries the death penalty, after riots earlier that month in which at least four people died.

However, when his trial began in December, prosecutors did not directly mention the riots -- the worst in Jakarta in 20 years. Instead, they accused Pakpahan of a number of subversive acts in his writings, speeches and trade union activities.

Visitors said Pakpahan remained under tight guard on Thursday at the Christian Cikini private hospital in central Jakarta where he was admitted late last Friday suffering from vertigo, a long-standing ailment.
Pakpahan, leader of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), had battled prison and court officials for the past three months to receive private treatment.
A medical source said X-rays and a scan on Monday revealed the presence of the tumour at the bottom of his right lung.
